sourcesNote: Trophy names, descriptions and grades are the official PS5 list as published. The guide text for every trophy is original to Leonida Legend, reasoned from the official description alone. Where the description does not pin down a location, count detail or step, the guide says so plainly instead of inventing one.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum itself, awarded automatically once the other fifty-four trophies are earned. There is nothing separate to hunt here: work the roadmap in order, clear the four missables before the finale, then finish the collectibles and grind stages. If this has not popped, use the checklist counts to find the one trophy still missing.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Simply finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission named in the official description. Treat this first pass as your tutorial for movement, driving and combat, because mission replay for trophies is not confirmed. Nothing here needs preparation, collectibles or money, so play it naturally, learn the controls, and let the story carry you into Leonida.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Complete every required mission in Chapter 1 and this unlocks as the chapter closes. While you are learning the map, bank the easy early activities nearby rather than rushing past them. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so handle any mission-specific action the story asks for on this first pass instead of assuming you can redo it later.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish all required missions in Chapter 2. By now the world should be opening up, so start noting activity types, shops and garages you pass for later completion work. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so complete any one-off action a mission presents on the first pass, and keep a manual save before major story beats as cheap insurance.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3 in full. This is a good point to pause between story missions and sample each activity type once, which quietly advances a separate trophy. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so treat set-piece moments as one-chance for any special action they offer, and keep rotating manual saves so a missed moment never costs the whole run.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the endgame stages of this roadmap. Before pushing further, clear any stranger strands you have opened and check the four missable trophies in this guide. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so do mission-specific actions first time, and save manually before committing to the final stretch of the story.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission to earn this gold trophy. Do not start it until the four missable trophies in Stage 4 are safely banked, because their one-chance moments sit before or around this point. Stock up, save manually in a separate slot, and go in prepared. Afterwards, free roam remains your home for collectibles, grinds and one hundred percent.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the named story mission Breakfast Run whenever it becomes available in the campaign. Follow its objectives through to the end rather than wandering off mid-mission. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so if the mission presents a distinctive vehicle, route or action, engage with it fully on this first pass instead of planning to return later.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, the named story mission in the official description. Heist-style missions reward preparation, so arrive with health, armour and suitable weapons topped up if the game allows it beforehand. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so play any unique heist action carefully first time, and keep a pre-mission manual save as your safety net.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the named story mission Child's Play from start to finish. The official description gives no extra conditions, so no medal, timer or no-damage requirement should be assumed. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so stay with the mission's own objectives and characters throughout, and avoid failing out at the final step by playing the closing section cautiously.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete Headliners, the named story mission. Simply seeing its credits moment is the requirement as published; no optional objective is stated. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so treat anything distinctive the mission puts in your hands as worth experiencing fully now. A manual save before starting costs nothing and protects you if anything goes wrong mid-mission.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown, the named story mission tied to the VCIA location that also features in a missable trophy elsewhere in this list. Finish the mission as directed, and note the area for later. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so handle mission-specific actions on the first pass and keep a separate save beforehand.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, the named story mission. The official description adds no side conditions, so focus purely on finishing it. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so if the operation hands you a special vehicle, weapon or escape route, use it as intended on this pass. Save manually before the mission marker to stay safe.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach one hundred percent completion as tracked by the game itself. This is the long tail of the platinum: story, strands, activities, collectibles and exploration all feed it. Work it last, using the in-game completion checklist if one is provided, because the official trophy description does not list which individual tasks count toward the percentage. Chase the missing percent, not guesses.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete two hundred and fifty stunts in total. This is a volume grind, so weave stunts into normal driving from early on instead of farming them all at the end. The official description does not say whether these are marked stunt jumps or any stunt the game registers, so follow the game's own stunt counter wherever it is displayed.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. The starter data notes nine activity types, so sample one of everything as activities unlock during Chapter 1 and beyond: a race, a range visit, an arcade game and so on. You only need a first attempt at each type, not a win, which makes this one of the cheapest early bankables in Leonida.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in every Shooting Range challenge; the starter data puts the total at forty-two challenges. Practise each weapon class until its scoring pattern feels routine, and replay challenges freely since ranges are built for repetition. The official description does not list per-challenge score targets, so read the target shown in game before each attempt and pace your shots accordingly.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location; the starter data counts fourteen locations. A win is required, not just participation, so learn each course with a sighting run first, then push for first place. The official description does not name the locations, so tick them off in this checklist as you discover and clear each one.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win twenty different races. The word different matters: repeating one easy race twenty times should not count, so keep moving to fresh events and mark each win here. Mix vehicle classes as new races unlock through the story. The official description does not specify race types, so any distinct race the game offers is worth winning once.

trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Find the fishing challenge involving Cal, learn its scoring or catch rules on a first attempt, then win the rematch with better bait, timing or catch selection as the game allows. The official description does not state where Cal fishes or what wins the challenge, so read the challenge's own rules screen carefully before starting.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Any cabinet you find early will do, which is why this sits in Stage 1 as an easy bankable. Completion is the requirement as published, not a high score, so pick the shortest or simplest game on offer. The official description does not name arcade locations, so use the first one the story or free roam shows you.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy, meaning work through Andy's whole stranger strand until its concluding mission, not just the first meeting. Strands usually chain several encounters, so return whenever a new Andy marker appears. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so finish each step properly on the first pass and keep the strand moving alongside the main story.

trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton by following Kenton's stranger strand through every encounter to its end. Do not mistake an early Kenton mission for the finale; the trophy needs the strand's last mission specifically. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so complete each step as it comes and revisit the map whenever Kenton's next marker appears.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy, the conclusion of Billy's stranger strand. Work each Billy encounter as it unlocks and keep returning until no new Billy mission appears, then finish the finale. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so treat each strand step as a first-pass job. This also counts toward the eight completed strands silver trophy.

trophies.guide: Complete eight full mission strands for strangers across Leonida. The named strands in this list, including Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone, are the obvious core, so finish those first and then complete additional strands you meet until the count reaches eight. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so track conclusions, not introductions, in this checklist.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy by playing Randy's stranger strand through to its conclusion. Keep checking back after each Randy encounter, since strand steps often unlock with time or story progress. Mission replay for trophies is not confirmed, so finish each step cleanly first time. Completing this strand also moves the eight-strands silver trophy one step closer.

trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone, closing out Tyrone's stranger strand in full. trophies.guide: Complete fifty challenges in total. Pick three shops close together, keep moving between them, and never let the police search fully expire until the third robbery is done. The official description does not name shops, so scout a tight cluster first and rehearse the route before committing to the run.

trophies.guide: The official description, a partnership with mass appeal, is deliberately vague and names no action, place or count. Honest advice is therefore limited: it most plausibly involves an activity done together with your partner that draws attention or a crowd. Try partner activities as they unlock, and if you discover its exact trigger in play, this trophy needs no grinding beyond that moment.

Save before major choices where the game allows, and keep playing naturally; the count should build across the campaign if you participate.
